stage1.impression: A warm, moody tabletop of a red acrylic turntable on a walnut cabinet against a salmon plaster wall, with a glowing red horn speaker cropped at left and a red lamp cropped at right. The material work on the walnut and the plaster is credible, but the wall is the brightest thing in the frame and the turntable sits darker than its background, its lower plinth sinking to near-black red while the record reads as smooth smoked glass. Everything is one red-pink, so the product does not separate, the cropped props pull the eye to the corners, and the flat frontal view onto a blank wall reads as a set, not a living room at dusk.

blocking_9: The turntable must be the brightest, most contrasty mass in the frame: product region lum_median above the wall's, and the wall behind it 30-40% darker than now
The wall must read near its specified off-white (delta_e to #EEE9E1 under 12 after white balance), so the acrylic's red is the only red and separates by hue
The lower plinth and pod must show light passing through the tinted acrylic (a glowing edge and caustic on the walnut), not crush to black-red (crush_pct near 0, lum_median above 40)
Visible depth of a living room at dusk: a soft, out-of-focus cool window or room recession in part of the background instead of a flat wall filling 60% of the frame
No half-cropped props at the frame edges: the speaker and lamp either read as deliberate, recognisable context or leave the frame
A defined contact shadow and red transmitted-light spill under the feet on the walnut
No over-sharpened or denoiser smear look on the plaster and record surface

defects.what: Wall is the brightest large area (lum_median 173) and renders salmon (RGB 226/160/141, delta_e 23.7 from the specified #EEE9E1); it out-shines the hero and tints the whole frame the product's colour
Lower plinth and motor pod crushed to near-black red (lum_median 15, G median 1, crush 2.8%); the tinted acrylic reads as opaque dark plastic, not light-transmitting
Record is a smooth smoky disc with no groove sheen or radial anisotropic highlight; reads as glass, not vinyl
Horn loudspeaker cropped to an unreadable sliver with hot pink LED panels (r_median 175, crush 4.75%); it is a distracting magenta block, not recognisable context
Lamp shade cropped at the top edge with clipped highlights (clip 0.88%); its own light barely registers on the turntable
Heavy black-red shadow blob on the wall from the speaker, saturated (G 17) and muddy
Feet are grey pucks with soft, weak contact shadows; the product looks set on rather than sitting with weight
Fluted cabinet front at the bottom edge has bright pale slats (p95 186) that pull the eye down and out of the frame
Plaster and record carry a smeared, over-sharpened denoiser look; everything says render on close inspection

changes.problem: The wall out-shines the product, so the hierarchy is inverted.

evidence.measured: wall lum_median 173 vs record/platter 71 and lower plinth 15

change.from: azimuth -35, elevation 10, distance 1.1, 0.6x0.4 m, 45 W, target z 0.74
change.to: azimuth -20, elevation 28, distance 0.9, 0.5x0.35 m, 60 W, target [0.36, 0.42, 0.72], with a spread/grid limiting it to the cabinet top (spot falloff so the wall above 1.0 m gets less than half)

changes.expected: The turntable top and acrylic edges lift to lum 100-140 while the wall falls into a gentle gradient, darker at the top.

changes.problem: The off-white wall renders salmon, so the product's red has no neutral ground to separate against.

change.to: 2800 (and lights.key color 2900 -> 3200) so the warm lamp light neutralises toward a warm cream instead of pink

changes.expected: Wall reads warm off-white/cream, the red acrylic is the only saturated red in the frame.

changes.problem: The lower plinth and pod crush to black-red; the tinted acrylic does not glow.

change.to: area 0.8x0.15 m behind and above the turntable at [0.36, 0.75, 0.95], aimed at [0.36, 0.42, 0.72], 25 W, 3000 K, camera-invisible, so light passes through the plinth sheets toward the lens

changes.expected: Plinth edges and pod light up as glowing red bands with transmitted light; red caustic spill on the walnut in front.

changes.problem: The speaker and lamp are cropped into unreadable coloured blocks that drag the eye to the edges.

evidence.measured: magenta sliver r_median 175, crush 4.75%; lamp clip 0.88% at top right

change.to: speaker moved back and left to [-0.9, 1.6, 0] (off the cabinet, deep in the room, defocused but whole in silhouette); lamp to [0.82, 0.55, 0.68] with the camera framing its full shade

changes.expected: The lamp reads as a whole object lighting the turntable; the speaker becomes a soft red silhouette in depth instead of a hard edge slab.

changes.problem: The flat, frontal view onto a blank wall gives no room depth and no dusk.

evidence.measured: wall fills the top 40% with lum_range 40 and no recession; window light colour #9FB4E0 never registers

change.to: [-0.25, -1.0, 1.02] -> [0.36, 0.42, 0.80], 75 mm, f/2.8, so the view runs diagonally along the cabinet with the window's cool dusk light and the room receding at left

changes.expected: A three-quarter view of the turntable with a soft blue-dusk background on one side and the warm lamp on the other; true depth of field.

changes.problem: The dusk window light is too weak to give the cool counterpoint the brief asks for.

evidence.measured: no cool tone anywhere in the frame: b_median below r_median in every region

changes.expected: Cool blue fill on the camera-left edges of the acrylic and the walnut, cool shadows against the warm lamp key.

changes.problem: The record reads as smoked glass, not vinyl.

evidence.measured: smooth gradient, no groove sheen; record is a set prop (set.props.2)

change.to: roughness 0.35 with concentric anisotropic groove normal (rotation radial, anisotropy 0.8) and a 3 mm smooth lead-in and run-out band

changes.expected: A radial bow-tie highlight across the record, crisp grooves where focus falls.

changes.problem: The pale fluted slats at the bottom edge pull the eye out of frame.

change.to: 0.86 (lift frame so the cabinet edge sits about 60 px from the bottom and the slats leave the frame)

changes.expected: The bottom of the frame ends on the dark walnut top edge.

out_of_scope.request: Make the platter and plinth tint slightly less saturated / more transparent so the acrylic reads as light passing through rather than dark red
out_of_scope.why: Product colour and material are fixed; handled here by backlighting (c3) instead

out_of_scope.request: Lighter feet or a visible isolation detail
